receipt.public_excerpt: Richard Sutton, recipient of the 2024 Turing Award, will argue that as “AI has become a huge industry, to an extent it has lost its way,” and proposes a return to fundamental principles

evidence_items.explanation: A Turing Award winner used a NeurIPS 2025 keynote on 3 December to say AI has 'lost its way' and needs different principles, consistent with major figures questioning the current approach.

receipt.public_excerpt: Despite rapid progress on benchmarks, state-of-the-art models still exhibit “jagged intelligence,” indicating that current scaling approaches may have limitations.

evidence_items.explanation: The Posner Lecture at NeurIPS 2025 (4 December) explicitly said current scaling approaches may have limits.

receipt.public_excerpt: All agreed that simply scaling today’s transformer models, giving them more data, more GPUs, and more training time, is no longer delivering meaningful returns.

evidence_items.explanation: A news report on the conference week (ending 7 December) describes researchers at NeurIPS 2025 as agreeing that pure scaling no longer pays off. It is a journalist's summary, not a count.

receipt.public_excerpt: Contra the popular belief that scaling is over—which we discussed in our NeurIPS ’25 talk with Ilya Sutskever and Quoc Le—the team delivered a drastic jump.

evidence_items.explanation: A major industry figure rejected the 'scaling is over' view just before the conference. This shows real dissent, though Marcus himself says not everyone agrees. His own wording, 'popular belief that scaling is over', suggests the skeptical view had spread.

unresolved_gaps: No source counts how many prominent figures held each view at NeurIPS 2025 compared with earlier years.
Sutton and Choi were not new converts; their talks show skepticism but not necessarily a change of mind.
